CESU settlement and SEPA commission-debit flow
CESU payment to commission collection flow
Clerk sign-up and Postgres sync flow

nodes.label: Clerk Responsibility Split (frontend vs API)
nodes.rationale: Sign-in and session UI stay on Next.js with @clerk/nextjs; the NestJS API owns registration, JWT verification, webhooks and Postgres RBAC. Frontends never POST credentials to the API to authenticate, so the API never handles passwords except at account creation.

nodes.label: Prisma baseline for TypeORM databases
nodes.rationale: db:resolve --applied marks existing migrations as applied without re-running DDL, so a database created by the former TypeORM migrations can adopt Prisma without dropping data.

nodes.label: apps/prisma.config.ts (Prisma 7)
nodes.rationale: Database URL, migrations path and seed command moved out of schema.prisma into the config file in ORM 7; seeding is explicit and no longer automatic after migrate.

nodes.label: SUPABASE_DB_MIGRATION_URL
nodes.rationale: Optional; the CLI falls back to SUPABASE_DB_URL when unset. On Railway, if the direct db.<ref>.supabase.co host is unreachable (P1001), the session pooler on 5432 is the substitute.

nodes.label: Container entrypoint runs migrate deploy
nodes.rationale: apps/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh runs prisma migrate deploy once per deploy using SUPABASE_DB_MIGRATION_URL before node dist/main.js, so schema and code ship together.

nodes.label: GET /health vs GET /ready
nodes.rationale: /health is liveness with no database and is what Railway probes; /ready pings Postgres through the runtime pooler URL and is for post-deploy smoke tests.

nodes.label: Railway PORT injection
nodes.rationale: Railway injects PORT and the app listens on API_PORT or PORT when API_PORT is unset, so API_PORT normally needs no manual value.

nodes.label: AdminGuard
nodes.rationale: Enforces the persisted UserRole.ADMIN after Clerk authentication, so authorization is decided in Postgres and not by the token.

nodes.label: CmsPage entity
nodes.rationale: Slug-keyed CMS row with jsonb structured columns and updatedByUserId as an audit pointer to the last admin editor.

nodes.label: ContentCmsModule (F19)
nodes.rationale: F19 was moved back out of the general ContentModule on 2026-05-21 to keep module boundaries clean: content-cms owns the concept page CMS only.

nodes.label: ContentModule (general content)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a placeholder for general app content so F19 CMS concerns do not leak into it.

nodes.label: GET /content/concept
nodes.rationale: Public, no ClerkAuthGuard.

nodes.label: PUT /content/concept
nodes.rationale: Admin-only; requires a Clerk token and UserRole.ADMIN.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage for CMS assets
nodes.rationale: SupabaseService is an optional client kept for future CMS asset uploads; binary upload is out of MVP scope.

nodes.label: UpdateConceptContentDto
nodes.rationale: Full replacement payload for admin saves rather than a patch, so a save is atomic and deterministic.

nodes.label: CESU migration not executed in the working environment
nodes.norm_label: cesu migration not executed in the working environment
nodes.rationale: No Postgres was reachable, so 20260905120000 must be run against a scratch database before deploying.

nodes.label: E0 — Prisma adoption
nodes.rationale: Baseline 20250522120000_init reproduces the former TypeORM DDL, so existing databases can be marked applied rather than rebuilt.

nodes.label: E1 — provider to chef rename
nodes.rationale: Enum and table renamed, but provider_id columns and a chefId API alias were intentionally kept so the existing booking flow does not break while terminology aligns.

nodes.label: Spec module to NestJS module traceability
nodes.norm_label: spec module to nestjs module traceability
nodes.rationale: Maps SPEC-BACKEND section 2.2 modules onto delivered NestJS modules; payments and content-cms are the only ones marked Done.

nodes.label: F19 exit criteria
nodes.rationale: All functional and non-regression cases passed or explicitly waived, evidence recorded in the execution log, and open questions resolved or converted into follow-ups.

nodes.label: Railway deployment of LF-BackEnd
nodes.rationale: Twelve-factor config in the Railway dashboard; Docker build from apps/Dockerfile per railway.toml, health check GET /health. The Compose postgres service is deliberately not deployed; Supabase is the database.

nodes.label: F19 functional test suite (F19-FUNC-001..010)
nodes.rationale: Covers public read, admin update, the 401/403 authorization matrix, DTO validation, deterministic defaults on a fresh database, and Swagger visibility.

nodes.label: F19 non-regression suite (F19-NR-001..006)
nodes.rationale: Test, build and lint plus health, readiness and an unauthenticated GET /bookings, so the CMS work cannot silently break the existing surface.

nodes.label: F19 functional cases blocked
nodes.rationale: All ten functional cases were Blocked at execution time because neither route, the admin guard, the DTOs nor the migration existed on the branch inspected.

nodes.label: F19 execution records
nodes.rationale: Baseline evidence from 2026-05-07: npm test, build and lint all passed after npm ci, with 3 suites and 13 tests.

nodes.label: RBAC in Postgres only
nodes.rationale: users.role in Postgres is the single source of truth; guards read the database, not Clerk metadata. Clerk proves identity and nothing more, so a compromised or stale Clerk publicMetadata cannot grant privileges.

nodes.label: Supabase RLS boundary
nodes.rationale: The API uses SUPABASE_DB_URL with Prisma as a service connection and never the Supabase JS client for users, so RLS applies only when a frontend talks to Supabase directly.

nodes.label: Idempotent migration rule
nodes.rationale: Prisma does not wrap a migration file in a transaction, so a mid-file failure commits everything before it and migrate deploy replays from the top into already-exists errors. Migrations touching pre-existing objects therefore use guarded DO blocks, IF EXISTS/IF NOT EXISTS and ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS.

nodes.label: Pooler vs direct connection split
nodes.rationale: Runtime Prisma and /ready use the transaction pooler (6543) while migrations use a direct or session connection (5432). Migrations must never run through the transaction pooler.

nodes.label: Public domain vs railway.internal
nodes.rationale: *.railway.internal is reachable only by other Railway services in the project; browsers, webhooks and curl need the generated public domain. Empty Swagger or /ready responses usually mean the internal hostname was used.

nodes.label: Deterministic concept defaults
nodes.rationale: concept-defaults.ts guarantees GET /content/concept answers on a fresh database before any admin has saved content.

nodes.label: Idempotent payments migrations
nodes.rationale: 20260831120000 failed mid-file twice during development, once on payment_status and once on payment_method, because Prisma runs migration files outside a transaction; every CREATE is now guarded and every ALTER uses IF EXISTS.

nodes.label: Resolved platform decisions (no re-litigation without ADR)
nodes.norm_label: resolved platform decisions (no re-litigation without adr)
nodes.rationale: ORM Prisma over TypeORM, Clerk over spec email/password JWT, bookings over spec reservation naming, chef over provider, Cronofy for calendar, Stream for messaging. Recorded so the spec's illustrative choices are not re-argued per epic.

nodes.label: Append-only execution log rule
nodes.rationale: A rerun adds a new row rather than replacing the old result, so the qualification history stays auditable.

nodes.label: Admin user provisioning routes
nodes.rationale: POST /admin/users and PATCH /admin/users/:id/role require a real CLERK_SECRET_KEY and answer 503 in local stub mode, because they must reach the Clerk Backend API.

nodes.label: ensurePersistedFromClerk
nodes.rationale: Upserts the users row from the JWT sub plus Clerk BAPI profile data. Called before role changes in PATCH /admin/users/:id/role so email, name and phone are present when elevating a user.

nodes.label: First admin bootstrap
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no self-serve promote-me-to-admin endpoint; the first admin is promoted by SQL, and subsequent roles via the admin route.

nodes.label: GET /me first sign-in sync
nodes.rationale: The primary Clerk to Postgres sync path; it works even when webhooks have not arrived, so the frontend must call it after every sign-in/sign-up before relying on LF user data.

nodes.label: Local Clerk stub mode (sk_test_placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Decode-only stub tokens, GET /me sourced from the JWT sub alone, admin provisioning 503, webhooks unverified. Lets the API run with no Clerk cloud dependency.

nodes.label: POST /webhooks/clerk
nodes.rationale: Svix-signed user.created/updated/deleted events verified with @clerk/backend verifyWebhook. Eventually consistent, so sign-in must never block on delivery.

nodes.label: db:backfill:clerk script
nodes.rationale: Pulls Clerk accounts created before the webhook existed, or that never hit GET /me. Writes require --yes; existing rows keep their role so a backfill cannot silently demote an admin; email conflicts on a different clerk_user_id are reported and skipped rather than failing on the unique index.

nodes.label: db:sync:clerk script
nodes.rationale: Postgres to Clerk direction for demo/placeholder clerk_user_id rows. There is no Clerk Dashboard action to import Supabase users, so a script is the only path.

nodes.label: Locally forged Clerk-like token
nodes.rationale: A base64url header and payload with a literal signature segment is enough in stub mode, which is what makes the authorization cases runnable without Clerk cloud.

nodes.label: Clerk BAPI email auto-verification gap
nodes.rationale: users.createUser auto-verifies email addresses, so both admin provisioning and public sign-up skip the Dashboard's frontend verification step. Nothing proves address ownership, so typo'd and disposable addresses reach users; rate limiting only blunts bulk abuse.

nodes.label: loadRepoEnv precedence trap
nodes.rationale: Repo-root .env.local overrides shell-exported variables, so exporting SUPABASE_DB_URL or CLERK_SECRET_KEY on the command line does not redirect the script. Always read the printed Database line before passing --yes.

nodes.label: Prefinanced CESU flow (e-CESU first)
nodes.rationale: Structurally different from card: the funds never transit through the platform. The client pays the chef directly from the issuer's beneficiary area, so nothing is programmatically verifiable and the commission cannot be withheld at charge time.

nodes.label: Mixed CESU + card coverage
nodes.rationale: coverage() counts succeeded payments only, never everything-not-failed, because an abandoned pending row would inflate coverage and a split booking would never reach confirmed. The card intent charges the remaining amount and refuses with 409 when nothing is left.

nodes.label: platformAttestedAmountCents
nodes.rationale: Excludes type B and e-CESU because the issuer already attests the share it financed. Flagged red: the medium is probably not the fiscally relevant axis, and attesting paper may carry the same over-declaration exposure under art. 199 sexdecies CGI. Open with the accountant; the fix is one line in isPlatformAttestable().

nodes.label: SAP declaration (sap_profiles)
nodes.rationale: Lives in UsersModule rather than PaymentsModule because it is self-declared profile data carrying no Stripe secrets. type_a_nova vs type_b_cooperative; switching type clears the other type's fields.

nodes.label: settlePayment() shared settlement
nodes.rationale: Extracted from the card handler as the sole writer of Payment.status succeeded, paidAt and taxCreditEligibleAmount, and owner of the booking transition, which is what makes a mixed CESU + card booking possible.

nodes.label: One fiscal attestation per issuing chef
nodes.norm_label: one fiscal attestation per issuing chef
nodes.rationale: Confirmed 2026-09-04: the chef is the declared prestataire, so a single client-level document covering several independent providers would not be valid. Client totals exist for dashboards only.

nodes.label: Booking confirmed only on payment_intent.succeeded
nodes.rationale: The API never trusts the client's confirmation result; only the webhook flips the booking to confirmed.

nodes.label: Chef confirms a CESU payment
nodes.rationale: No issuer exposes an API and no transaction reference is normalised, so the chef, the only party receiving both the issuer notification and the money, is the confirming authority, with a traced admin force-settle requiring a proof reference for support cases.

nodes.label: CRCESU NAN publication
nodes.rationale: The NAN must be published on the public chef profile, the booking detail and each quote because a client cannot add the chef on their issuer portal without it, and invoice A arrives far too late to be the sole carrier.

nodes.label: No self-declared habilitation
nodes.rationale: urssafTiersPrestationStatus and crcesuAffiliationStatus are absent from the update DTO by design, the same rule as isActive/isVerified: a chef must not declare themselves habilitated.

nodes.label: CRCESU no-surcharge rule enforced structurally
nodes.rationale: Commission is computed per payment line with no proportional split, a declaration can never exceed what is due, and there is no fee field anywhere on the CESU path.

nodes.label: Paper CESU deliberately unmanaged
nodes.rationale: The platform provides the payment method, the invoice and the commission debit; depositing, validating and cashing the titres is the chef's responsibility. No chef-facing contractual document exists yet, so the clause has nowhere to live.

nodes.label: Partial unique index on live CESU payments
nodes.norm_label: partial unique index on live cesu payments
nodes.rationale: payments (booking_id) WHERE method = cesu AND status <> failed holds concurrency: two simultaneous declarations would each pass the coverage check. Prisma cannot express a partial index, so it exists only in the migration.

nodes.label: Production blockers checklist
nodes.rationale: Enumerates what the operator must supply before go-live: Supabase pooler+direct strings, production Clerk key, Stripe live keys with Connect enabled, both webhook endpoints and their secrets, and the negotiated commission rate (the 15% default is a placeholder).

nodes.label: CORS_ORIGINS override
nodes.rationale: Product frontends are already allowlisted in apps/src/config/allowed-origins.ts; the variable exists only for preview deploys, tunnels and staging. Exact scheme+host+port, no wildcards.

nodes.label: Basis-point commission with frozen rates
nodes.rationale: Integer arithmetic avoids float drift, and freezing rate_bps/vat_rate_bps on the commissions row means a later rate change can never rewrite history or break an audit replay.

nodes.label: Stripe Connect destination charge
nodes.rationale: Chosen so the commission is withheld as application_fee_amount at charge time: collected atomically with the payment, no payout job and no second debit.

nodes.label: Express Connect account (FR)
nodes.rationale: Capabilities card_payments + transfers so Stripe hosts KYC; business_type is left unset so the hosted form can ask whether the chef is a micro-entreprise or a company.

nodes.label: Commission configuration (bps)
nodes.rationale: PAYMENTS_COMMISSION_RATE_BPS defaults to 1500 (the contracted 15% HT) and PAYMENTS_COMMISSION_VAT_RATE_BPS to 2000; both are bounded to 0..10000 in env.validation.ts and frozen onto each commission row.

nodes.label: computeCommission()
nodes.rationale: VAT is computed from the rounded HT amount so HT + VAT === TTC always holds; the total is clamped to the charge because Stripe rejects a fee larger than the charge and a misconfigured rate must not fail every payment; a zero commission sends no application_fee_amount at all.

nodes.label: POST /payments/intent
nodes.rationale: Returns a client_secret so the backend never sees card details. Answers 409 when the booking is not pending, already paid, the chef's Connect onboarding is incomplete, or the amount is not positive.

nodes.label: Legacy payments rows deleted by backfill
nodes.norm_label: legacy payments rows deleted by backfill
nodes.rationale: The backfill attaches old rows via bookings.payment_id then bookings.stripe_payment_intent_id; anything matching neither is deleted because booking_id is NOT NULL. Check a production dump before deploying.

nodes.label: payments 1:N bookings
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not 1:1: a failed card attempt must be retryable with a fresh PaymentIntent, so a booking may carry several payment rows and the most recent non-failed row is the live attempt.

nodes.label: PaymentIntent reuse idempotency
nodes.rationale: A second call returns the existing pending intent instead of creating another; an intent that can no longer be confirmed is dropped and replaced; and if Stripe already reports succeeded while the webhook is in flight the call answers 409 rather than double-billing.

nodes.label: SEPA mandate (CORE)
nodes.rationale: Recorded but never debited in the card phase; groundwork for avance immediate and CESU where the fee cannot be split at charge time. Only the IBAN last four digits are persisted; the IBAN itself never reaches the backend.

nodes.label: Local stripe listen workflow
nodes.rationale: stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/webhooks/stripe prints the whsec secret for repo-root .env; the .env.local precedence warning applies.

nodes.label: POST /webhooks/stripe
nodes.rationale: Public and unauthenticated, verified by the stripe-signature header. Excluded from Swagger with @ApiExcludeController; anything unhandled is logged at debug and ignored.

nodes.label: SEPA mandate SetupIntent routes
nodes.rationale: The frontend collects the IBAN with Stripe Elements and confirms the SetupIntent there, so the IBAN never reaches the backend; setup_intent.succeeded stores the mandate id and ibanLast4.

nodes.label: Chef Stripe Connect onboarding routes
nodes.rationale: Account links are single-use and short-lived so the URL must never be cached; status reads the Postgres flags mirrored from account.updated rather than the Stripe API, so the frontend can poll it cheaply.

nodes.label: 56-day clawback window
nodes.rationale: CommissionDebit.clawbackWindowEndsAt models the CORE revocation period as a hard-coded constant, deliberately not configurable: it is the scheme's rule, not the platform's, and a variable invites someone to fix a non-conformity by editing a value.

nodes.label: Payability gate (chargesEnabled and payoutsEnabled)
nodes.rationale: A booking whose chef has not finished onboarding answers 409, so the chef's onboarding state must be surfaced in the chef app before a client ever reaches checkout.

nodes.label: Raw-body signature verification
nodes.rationale: A Fastify preParsing hook in apps/src/main.ts captures the raw bytes for the paths listed in fastify-raw-body.ts, because a re-serialised JSON body fails Stripe's signature check.

nodes.label: Refunds as passive bookkeeping
nodes.rationale: Commission.status is deliberately untouched on a refund because Stripe does not refund the application_fee_amount unless asked, so the commission really was collected. Clawing it back belongs to an admin refund flow that does not exist.

nodes.label: SEPA commission-debit engine
nodes.rationale: Webhook-driven because SEPA never answers succeeded synchronously; N attempts per invoice, a 10000 EUR cap, and a recorded clawback window. Deferred out of the card phase and reusable unchanged for the avance immediate.

nodes.label: Commission invoice (facture B)
nodes.rationale: Issued before any debit because it is the legal basis of the collection: the prelevement is made against the invoice, not against a raw application_fee_amount. Numbered LF-COM-<year>-NNNN; PDF and S3 archival belong to the invoicing workstream.

nodes.label: Service invoice A (prestataire-named)
nodes.rationale: Client-facing, issued in the chef's name by the platform on their behalf, showing the booking's payment method. Trigger is still open: payment_intent.succeeded means charged, not delivered.

nodes.label: No on_behalf_of on the commission debit
nodes.norm_label: no on_behalf_of on the commission debit
nodes.rationale: The platform is the seller on facture B, and on_behalf_of, transfer_data or application_fee_amount would invalidate the already-collected mandate by forcing a fresh authorisation. A dedicated test asserts their absence.

nodes.label: No cron scheduler
nodes.rationale: The repo has none, and with the debit triggered on confirmation and no titre reimbursement to follow, nothing time-based is mandatory: the monthly batch and debit retries are admin endpoints, advisory-locked for multi-instance Railway.

nodes.label: on_behalf_of for invoice A seller-of-record
nodes.rationale: Resolved 2026-09-05: adding on_behalf_of to the existing destination charge makes the connected account merchant of record with one parameter, no switch to direct charges. Express chef accounts already hold card_payments, which requires the full service agreement, so no re-onboarding. Not implemented yet.

nodes.label: S3 write-only invoice archival
nodes.rationale: S3 holds only a private copy for the 10-year Code de commerce retention; neither party is ever served from it, so the object key is recorded in Postgres against the owning row.

nodes.label: SEPA CORE scheme constraint
nodes.rationale: Stripe exposes only the CORE scheme, so the mandat SEPA B2B named in the commercial documentation is not buildable. CORE's no-questions-asked 8-week dispute right is honoured automatically, which drives the reversed state and the booking block.

nodes.label: Unpaid-commission guard
nodes.rationale: Booking creation and both payment paths refuse 409 for a chef with an invoice out of debit attempts or a commission reversed after a dispute. It is the counterweight to accepting CORE: rather than making an eight-week revocable debit safe, the exposure is capped at what is already owed.

nodes.label: Chef vetting flags (is_active / is_verified)
nodes.rationale: Self-registered chefs are always created inactive and unverified and neither field is accepted by PATCH /me/chef-profile, so a chef cannot self-habilitate. Only PATCH /admin/chefs/:id/verification may flip them. Known gap: no code reads the flags yet.

nodes.label: POST /auth/register
nodes.rationale: The only unauthenticated write endpoint; IP rate-limited via REGISTER_THROTTLE_LIMIT (default 5/hour) because it creates real Clerk accounts. Reversed a prior out-of-scope decision on 2026-08-03 because the product needs self-serve sign-up before booking.

nodes.label: Sign-in ticket (signInToken)
nodes.rationale: Single-use, 60s TTL (CLERK_SIGN_IN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS). Treated as a credential: redeem immediately, never log, persist, or place in a URL. It lets the API own sign-up while Clerk still establishes the session.

nodes.label: Two-step sign-up flow
nodes.rationale: Form 1 creates the account, form 2 fills the client or chef profile after the Clerk session exists, so profile data is written under an authenticated identity.

nodes.label: Profile type switch blocked with 409
nodes.rationale: Switching client to chef after onboarding is refused because reconciling the orphaned profile, bookings and payouts is real work planned separately.

nodes.label: Route-selects-the-role rule
nodes.rationale: role is absent from every DTO on the sign-up path, so forbidNonWhitelisted turns a submitted role into 400. A sign-up form may show a client/chef choice but must map it to the endpoint, never to a body field; admin has no public surface at all.

nodes.label: Reversal of the auth/register out-of-scope decision
nodes.norm_label: reversal of the auth/register out-of-scope decision
nodes.rationale: Recorded 2026-08-03: the product needs self-serve sign-up before booking, so the API owns registration while Clerk keeps sign-in. Sign-in, refresh and logout stay off the API.

nodes.label: Auth routes intentionally out of scope
nodes.norm_label: auth routes intentionally out of scope
nodes.rationale: POST /auth/login, /refresh and /logout stay off the API because Clerk owns sign-in and session lifecycle on the Next.js frontend.

nodes.label: E2 — Bookings lifecycle
nodes.rationale: POST /bookings replaced its 501 scaffold, which is breaking for callers that asserted 501. Lifecycle states shopping/cooking/delivered and the booking_meals junction remain Todo.

nodes.label: E8 — Payments epic
nodes.rationale: Delivered in two waves: card/Connect/commissions on 2026-08-31, prefinanced CESU and the SEPA commission-debit engine on 2026-09-05.

nodes.label: sepa_debit PaymentIntents never return succeeded
nodes.rationale: paymentIntents.create on sepa_debit returns processing and a late failure surfaces as requires_payment_method, since a PaymentIntent has no failed status. The API response is therefore only recorded, never trusted.

nodes.label: StripeEventLog de-duplication on processedAt
nodes.rationale: The guard tests processedAt rather than row existence: a handler that throws has already inserted its row, so an existence check would read Stripe's retry, the one chance to get the event right, as a duplicate and lose it permanently.

nodes.label: Webhook routing by database lookup
nodes.rationale: Never discriminate on metadata: a Dispute carries empty metadata and a Mandate has none, so metadata routing silently misfiles exactly the events that matter. A CommissionDebit lookup on stripePaymentIntentId decides between the commission engine and the client flow.

nodes.label: Admin list pagination breaking change
nodes.rationale: GET /admin/clients now returns { data, meta } instead of a bare array; shared primitives live in apps/src/common/dto/pagination.dto.ts for the other admin lists.

nodes.label: Unvetted chef is payable (money-bearing gap)
nodes.rationale: is_active and is_verified are still read nowhere, so a self-registered chef who completes Stripe Connect onboarding can be paid. Chef listings, booking assignment and any future ChefGuard must filter on both.

nodes.label: Webhook handler idempotency
nodes.rationale: Stripe delivers at least once and retries anything not 2xx, so every handler is a no-op on redelivery: a settled payment is skipped, a late payment_failed cannot undo it, an unchanged refund is not rewritten, and account.updated is an updateMany keyed on the account id.

nodes.label: AdminGuard (persisted admin role)
nodes.rationale: Admin authority is the persisted UserRole.ADMIN in Postgres, not a Clerk claim, so revoking admin does not depend on token refresh.

nodes.label: ApplicationDocument entity
nodes.rationale: Documents (CV, HACCP, diploma, ID) live in object storage and are served through signed access, never as public URLs — hence a dedicated GET /admin/applications/:id/documents/:docId download route.

nodes.label: chef role replaces provider
nodes.rationale: E1 migration renamed the provider role to chef; provider_id columns are kept temporarily for compatibility rather than dropped in the same migration.

nodes.label: Clerk as the identity provider
nodes.rationale: The spec asked for first-party JWT + refresh tokens; the implementation delegates to Clerk instead, so there are no /auth/register or password routes in the API and every protected route consumes a Clerk-issued JWT. Sign-in/sign-up stay on the Next.js frontends.

nodes.label: Payments data model (ER)
nodes.rationale: payments is not unique on booking_id; commissions is 1:1 with a payment and denormalises chef_profile_id because commission generated by chef X is a recurring admin query; payments.metadata is a deliberate extension slot for the avance immediate and CESU flows.

nodes.label: Fiscal attestation routes
nodes.rationale: Only succeeded payments count and the tax year is decided by paidAt, not createdAt, so an intent created on 31 December and settled on 1 January belongs to the later year and a refund drops out on its own. JSON only, no signed PDF.

nodes.label: GET/PATCH /me/chef-profile/sap
nodes.rationale: Upsert living in UsersModule, not PaymentsModule; switching declarationType clears the other type's fields so a cooperative chef cannot keep a stale NOVA code.

nodes.label: 50% SAP tax credit (amountAfterTax)
nodes.rationale: POST /bookings persists amountAfterTax = amountTtc / 2 per SPEC-BACKEND section 4.3.

nodes.label: payment_status paid reserved and unset
nodes.rationale: paid is kept for the invoiceable step and no code path sets it; the implemented flow is pending to succeeded.

nodes.label: Admin console mirrors the client space
nodes.norm_label: admin console mirrors the client space
nodes.rationale: Every client-facing feature has a matching management feature (book a session / manage all bookings, ask for a custom quote / price and send it, review left / review moderated) — the mirror is the organising principle for the console's module list.

nodes.label: One API and one database for three frontends
nodes.norm_label: one api and one database for three frontends
nodes.rationale: The vitrine site, the client space and the admin console share a single backend and a single database; the main site feeds the backend (contact forms, chef applications, Kossam orders) rather than owning its own store.

nodes.label: Liveness and readiness checks
nodes.rationale: GET /health is deliberately dependency-free (liveness) while GET /ready pings Postgres, so an orchestrator can distinguish a dead process from a degraded dependency.

nodes.label: Prisma as the ORM
nodes.rationale: Prisma (PrismaService + apps/prisma/schema.prisma) was chosen over the spec's open 'Prisma ORM' suggestion and over TypeORM; migrations run via `prisma migrate deploy` in the API container entrypoint so a deploy is always schema-correct before the process boots.

nodes.label: Dev/prod parity test environment
nodes.rationale: The test environment uses the same backing services as local development to preserve parity.

nodes.label: Booking lifecycle state machine
nodes.rationale: POST /bookings creates a booking as pending; the only automatic transition wired is pending -> confirmed driven by the Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook, because the API must never confirm a booking on the client's word. A failed payment deliberately leaves the booking pending so the client can retry.

nodes.label: vX.Y.Z version scheme
nodes.rationale: X = major/epic release with breaking changes, Y = backward-compatible feature release, Z = fixes and security patches.

nodes.label: Admin clients pagination contract
nodes.rationale: limit is capped at 100 and the response carries a meta envelope (page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNextPage, hasPreviousPage) so the console never has to infer paging state.

nodes.label: Quote lifecycle (submitted → accepted)
nodes.rationale: submitted → in-review → quoted → accepted (or declined); accepting a quote may generate a reservation.

nodes.label: Reservation lifecycle (pending → delivered)
nodes.rationale: pending → confirmed → shopping → cooking → delivered with a cancelled branch; a reference LF-AAAA-NNNN is generated at creation and each transition fires a notification.

nodes.label: Shopping list generation by aisle
nodes.rationale: Ingredients from the selected meals are aggregated per aisle and scaled to the portion count; one shopping-lists service serves both the client space and the admin console.

nodes.label: 50% SAP tax credit (crédit d'impôt)
nodes.rationale: The personal-services tax credit is 50%, so both amountTTC and amountAfterTax = amountTTC / 2 are stored rather than recomputed at render time.

nodes.label: Release register
nodes.rationale: Keeps the pre-release approval date on or before the release date to preserve an audit trail; v2.1.0 records the Stripe CB payments epic (Connect destination charges, platform commission, SAP/SEPA foundations, fiscal attestations, POST /bookings).

nodes.label: Booking aggregate naming (bookings vs reservation)
nodes.rationale: The spec's 'reservation' maps onto the pre-existing `bookings` module and table; renaming was rejected as churn, so implementation keeps /bookings paths unless a versioned alias is added later.

nodes.label: Routing payment_intent events by commission_debits lookup
nodes.norm_label: routing payment_intent events by commission_debits lookup
nodes.rationale: A payment_intent event is routed to the commission engine or the client flow by looking the intent up in commission_debits — never by metadata, which a Dispute leaves empty and a Mandate does not carry at all.

nodes.label: Commission invoiced as facture B
nodes.rationale: Because the commission cannot be withheld at charge time on CESU, it is invoiced as facture B (commission_invoices, LF-COM-<year>-NNNN) and collected by SEPA direct debit. The invoice always precedes the debit — it is the legal basis the debit collects against — and a failed debit adds an attempt without cancelling the receivable, so invoice numbers never develop holes.

nodes.label: Prefinanced CESU settlement
nodes.rationale: On a prefinanced CESU payment the funds never transit through the platform: the client pays from the issuer's beneficiary area using the chef's CRCESU number (NAN) and the issuer credits the chef directly. No issuer exposes an API, so nothing is programmatically verifiable and the chef must confirm receipt, with a traced admin override as the escape hatch.

nodes.label: Raw-body webhook signature verification
nodes.rationale: POST /webhooks/clerk and POST /webhooks/stripe are public but signature-verified against the raw request bytes; a Fastify preParsing hook in main.ts captures them for a fixed path list because a re-serialised JSON body would fail verification.

nodes.label: SEPA CORE 8-week clawback window
nodes.rationale: Stripe supports only the SEPA CORE scheme (not B2B), so a debit stays revocable 'no questions asked' for 8 weeks; that deadline is materialised on commission_debits.clawback_window_ends_at rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Stripe Connect destination charge
nodes.rationale: A card payment is a Connect destination charge: the platform keeps the commission as application_fee_amount and the chef's connected account receives the rest, so the commission is collected atomically at charge time and never has to be invoiced back.

nodes.label: stripe_event_logs webhook de-duplication
nodes.rationale: Stripe re-delivers events, so stripe_event_logs de-duplicates on processed_at rather than on mere row existence — a row that was inserted but not finished must still be reprocessed.

nodes.label: Uncollectable commission blocks a chef
nodes.rationale: A chef whose commission cannot be collected stops receiving bookings and payments — the platform's only leverage once the money has bypassed it entirely.

nodes.label: lib/mock as the backend integration seam
nodes.norm_label: lib/mock as the backend integration seam
nodes.rationale: The console ships fully built on mock data; each mock file maps one-to-one onto an API resource, so wiring the backend means swapping lib/mock/* imports for a lib/api/ client instead of rewriting pages.
